method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Chronic abdominal pain = intermittent or constant pain present for at least two months.** In most children no organic cause is found.
claims.source_text: Chronic abdominal pain is intermittent or constant abdominal pain that has been present for at least two months … In most children, no organic cause is found
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Organic and functional causes are not mutually exclusive** — they can coexist and interact.
claims.source_text: The aetiology may be organic or functional. These are not mutually exclusive; they can exist alongside each other and interact
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Comorbid anxiety and depression are very common**, and may both result from and contribute to chronic pain.
claims.source_text: Comorbid mental health issues (including anxiety and depression) are very common in children with chronic abdominal pain. These may both result from, and contribute to, the experience of chronic pain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ask about associated symptoms:** unintentional weight loss or stunting · unexplained fever · change in bowel habit, chronic diarrhoea or blood in stools · nocturnal stooling · appetite change · dysphagia or odynophagia · persistent (especially bilious) vomiting · urinary symptoms · extraintestinal features of IBD.
claims.source_text: unintentional weight loss/stunting of height unexplained fever changes in bowel habit, chronic diarrhoea, blood in stools nocturnal stooling appetite changes dysphagia … odynophagia (pain on swallowing) persistent vomiting (especially if bilious. See acute abdominal pain) urinary symptoms extraintestinal manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) (eyes, skin, joints, perianal)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also ask** about reflux symptoms, diet (including excluded foods), menstrual and sexual history where relevant, family history of IBD or coeliac disease, a HEADSSS screen and the **functional impact on school and activities**.
claims.source_text: History of reflux symptoms (heartburn, waterbrash, regurgitation) Dietary history (including foods excluded from diet) Menstrual history, sexual history and contraception (if relevant) Family history of IBD or coeliac disease HEADSSS screen Functional impact of pain on usual activities (eg school attendance, social activities, physical activity)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine:** hydration, weight and height (preferably over time), pubertal status, abdomen for palpable faeces or mass, and extraintestinal signs of IBD.
claims.source_text: Signs of dehydration Weight and height, preferably over time Pubertal status Abdominal examination for palpable faeces, palpable mass Extraintestinal manifestations of IBD
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Organic causes are more likely if there are red flags.**
claims.source_text: More likely if there are red flags
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Coeliac disease:** altered bowel habit, poor weight gain or slow growth, treatment-resistant iron deficiency, bloating, family history.
claims.source_text: Coeliac disease Altered bowel habit Poor weight gain or slow growth Anaemia/iron deficiency (treatment resistant) Bloating Family history of coeliac disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Irritable bowel syndrome:** pain at least 4 days per month with a change in bowel habit, or related to defecation.
claims.source_text: Irritable bowel syndrome Abdominal pain at least 4 days per month, associated with change in bowel habit Pain associated with change in frequency or form of stool Pain related to defecation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Abdominal migraine:** stereotyped paroxysmal periumbilical or diffuse pain with few or no GI symptoms between attacks; migraine in the child or family.
claims.source_text: Abdominal migraine Stereotypical, paroxysmal episodes of periumbilical or diffuse abdominal pain with few or no GI complaints between attacks Migraine in child (or family)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Functional dyspepsia:** postprandial fullness, early satiety, epigastric pain or burning unrelated to bowel habit.
claims.source_text: Functional dyspepsia Bothersome postprandial fullness Early satiety Epigastric pain and burning not associated with bowel habit
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Many children need no investigations**; target any testing to the likely diagnosis.
claims.source_text: Many children do not need investigations … Investigations should be targeted to likely diagnoses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Faecal calprotectin for children over 4 years with IBD features.** Do not test under 4 years without discussing with a paediatrician or paediatric gastroenterologist.
claims.source_text: faecal calprotectin for children over 4 years (if features of IBD). Do not test under the age of 4 years without discussion with a paediatrician or paediatric gastroenterologist
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods, if indicated:** UEC, LFTs, CMP, lipase, TSH, glucose, coeliac serology with total IgA, ESR/CRP, FBE and ferritin.
claims.source_text: blood: UEC, LFTs, CMP, lipase, TSH, blood sugar, coeliac serology and total IgA level, inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), FBE & ferritin
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imaging is not routinely required**; abdominal ultrasound has very low yield, though it may exclude a mass when examination is abnormal or there are significant constitutional symptoms.
claims.source_text: imaging is not routinely required abdominal ultrasound has very low yield in childhood chronic abdominal pain it may be useful in excluding an intra-abdominal mass for children with abnormal examination or significant constitutional symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not perform abdominal X-rays for non-specific abdominal pain** — they are rarely helpful even for constipation.
claims.source_text: do not perform abdominal X-rays for investigation of non-specific abdominal pain. Abdominal X-rays are rarely helpful in diagnosing constipation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test for *H. pylori* only with peptic-ulcer red flags**, by stool antigen or urease breath test. **Do not use *H. pylori* serology.**
claims.source_text: Only test for H. pylori (by stool antigen or urease breath test) if there are red flags for peptic ulcer disease (eg haematemesis, family history of H. pylori complication). Do not test H. pylori serology
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reflux symptoms in older children and adolescents: a 4-week PPI trial before referral may help.** Refer if not responding or unable to wean.
claims.source_text: For older children and adolescents with reflux symptoms, a 4-week trial of proton pump inhibitor (PPI) pre-referral may be helpful. Refer to a specialist if not responding appropriately or unable to wean PPI
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected IBD: seek specialist advice and refer to paediatric gastroenterology.**
claims.source_text: If IBD is suspected, seek specialist advice, and refer to paediatric gastroenterology
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Functional pain:** educate and reassure (no physical damage; most resolve with time and support); further tests and medicines are usually not needed; address psychosocial stressors.
claims.source_text: Education and reassurance for the child and parents. There is no physical damage to treat, and most cases will resolve with time and support Further investigations and medications are usually not required Consider and address psychosocial stressors
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen for comorbid anxiety or depression** and consider mental health referral; **encourage return to function** (school, social, physical activity) and provide follow-up.
claims.source_text: Consider comorbid anxiety or depression. If present, discuss with the child/young person and family and consider referral to mental health team or psychologist … Encourage a focus on return to function: continuing or graded return to usual activities (school, social, extra-curricular, physical activity) Provide follow-up
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IBS, abdominal migraine, functional dyspepsia: refer to a specialist** for CBT/psychology, specialist dietitian input, gut-directed hypnotherapy, or medicines such as SSRI/low-dose TCA and antispasmodics. **No diet changes without professional advice.**
claims.source_text: For specific functional abdominal pain disorders (IBS, abdominal migraine, functional dyspepsia), referral to a specialist for consideration of evidence-based treatments, which include: Psychology/Cognitive Behavioural Therapy/counselling Specialist dietician input to discuss evidence-based dietary strategies Changes to diet should not be undertaken without professional advice Gut-directed hypnotherapy Use of medications such as antidepressants (SSRI/low dose TCA) and antispasmodics
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Significant functional impairment** (poor school attendance, depression or anxiety, sleep disturbance): consider a paediatrician, adolescent medicine or a paediatric chronic pain service.
claims.source_text: If there is significant functional impairment (eg poor school attendance, concurrent depression or anxiety, sleep disturbance), consider referral to a paediatrician, adolescent medicine or a paediatric chronic pain management service
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** if the child needs admission, has red flags or abnormal investigations.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Child requiring admission Red flags or abnormal investigations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** when there are no concerning features, red flags have been considered **and** a clear follow-up plan is arranged.
claims.source_text: There are no concerning clinical features and red flags have been considered AND A clear follow-up plan has been arranged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23
